messages:
maria (frontend): noticing much slower chart handoff since 8.3.1 rollout. lots of long tasks during initial page load on dashboards with many widgets. LCP/Tti regressed by ~600ms on my canary.

sam (eng-platform): thanks for flagging — any idea what changed in the bundle or prefetch path this week?

maria (frontend): quick diff shows vendor grew ~140KB gzipped. PRs merged this week pulled in a synchronous crypto helper and an analytics shim into vendor.

jordan (sre): traces show parse/compile time is the main culprit; long task count up, GC modest. also seeing increased KV prefetch misses for route-prefetch keys.

kai (devex): I instrumented a sample: when prefetch fires aggressively we create >20 concurrent fetches, parsing them blocks main thread. small pages are fine, heavy dashboards hit the parse backlog.

sam (eng-platform): did we change prefetch strategy? last week's change made route prefetch immediate to reduce tail for TG routes.

maria (frontend): yes, PR #7301 moved from "prefetch on idle" to "prefetch on route enter". the intent was to avoid tail when switching routes, but side-effect is more parallel work during initial route hydation.

jordan (sre): immediate prefetch + larger vendor = win for some flows but overall regress for dense dashboards. we should throttle prefetch concurrency or revert as a quick safety.

maria (frontend): short-term I'd like to revert the prefetch heuristic (hotfix) and then run two experiments: 1) chunk vendor to async for heavy deps + lazy dynamic import for chart libs; 2) keep the prefetch but gate it with a "deferOnBusy" rule that checks main thread long task count.

kai (devex): sketched a patch for deferOnBusy:

```js
function shouldPrefetch() {
  if (performance.longTaskCount > 3) return false;
  if (prefetchInflight > 8) return false;
  return true;
}
```

and a dynamic import suggestion for charts.

maria (frontend): also propose a webpack cacheGroup that isolates `crypto-utils` as async so it doesn't land in vendor initial.

sam (eng-platform): let's do immediate revert as mitigation, then canary A/B the two strategies. we need telemetry labels to compare: per-route TTI, long task count, vendorParseTime, prefetch_hit_rate.

kai (devex): I'll add temporary metrics: `console_vendor_parse_ms`, `prefetch_concurrency`, and `prefetch.blocked_by_busy`. will increase sampling for the canary cohort.

jordan (sre): deploy-bot: request rollback approved. rolling back console frontend canary 8.3.1 -> 8.3.0 for 15% cohort. initiated at 14:09 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollback started; ETA ~4m.

maria (frontend): PRs: revert -> #7310, async-split+lazy -> #7315. telemetry dashboard: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/dashboards/prefetch_canary_check

sam (eng-platform): once rollback lands, we'll wait ~30m for new telemetry then spin the A/B. note: be mindful of request overhead if we create many small chunks.

kai (devex): added alert: `vendor_gzip_bytes > 780000 => #perf` and checklist item in rollout guide about prefetch concurrency and vendor budget.

maria (frontend): thanks — I'll follow up with perf numbers and the canary assignment.

sam (eng-platform): thanks team. keep updates here and paste the perf dashboard links.
